prerequisites: Differential and integral calculus for functions of one and several real variables

learning_outcomes.text: It is desired that the student acquires the ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering by applying the knowledge acquired on differential and integral calculus, ordinary and partial differential equations, and numerical methods.

syllabus_topics: Complex numbers. Sums and products. Basic algebraic properties. Complex conjugates. Moduli. Polar form. Powers. Roots of complex numbers.
Analytic functions. Functions of a complex variable. Mappings. Limits. Continuity. Derivatives. Cauchy-Riemann equations. Analytic functions. Harmonic functions.
Elementary functions. The exponential function. Trigonometric functions. The logarithmic function. Complex exponents. Hyperbolic functions.
Integrals. Definite integrals of complex functions of a real variable. Contour integrals. Antiderivatives. The Cauchy-Goursat theorem. The Cauchy integral formula.
Series. Taylor series. Laurent series. z-transform. Fourier series.
Second order linear homogeneous equations with constant coefficients.

assessment_methods.method: Final exam on Complex Variables (part of December exam)
Final exam on Differential Equations (part of December exam)

assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, an October exam on Complex Variables is worth 4 points. A December exam covers the entire course: Complex Variables (4 points) and Differential Equations (6 points). The final grade is the maximum of (December exam score) or (October exam score + Differential Equations part of the December exam). In the extraordinary call, a single exam similar to the December exam will be held in January, and its score will be the student's final grade.
